reflection.text:
This was a correct call - unblinded as AZ-J, truth Epithelial, agent Epithelial p=0.68 - but the path mattered because several features were traps for an Aurora/microtubule read.

What got it right:

1. Acquisition strategy: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.003-10uM with 4 wells available. We sampled the dynamic range intentionally: high dose w_eefdd61b1d1d 10uM [e2], mid doses w_0b5df1d0ab 0.3uM [e3] and w_443392cc3e 1uM [e7], and low dose w_033a39b2df 0.03uM [e8]. That bracketing let us test dose-dependence rather than a single-dose snapshot.

2. The load-bearing evidence was compare_to_reference_atlas. Both the 2-well vote [e6] and the 4-well vote [e9] were Epithelial 4/4 by NSC with k-neighbour split Epithelial 5/10, Protein synthesis 4/10, Eg5 1/10. The Epithelial prior persisted across doses with similarity 0.71-0.86 noted in rationale. That stability is why we did not chase the single-feature signal.

3. The single-feature signal that could have misled was frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+8.0 at 10uM [e2], +9.0 at 0.3uM [e3], +10.9 at 1uM [e7] plus nuc_eccentricity z~+7.5-7.9 and nuc_major_axis z negative. Taken alone that mimics cytokinesis failure / Aurora phenotype, which microscopist also flagged as candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors [e4][e5] with density lower vs DMSO. Multinucleation after Aurora-A loss is known from literature PMID 30050055 and Aurora A/B inhibition effects PMID 40195468, so the hypothesis was not implausible.

4. Dose_response broke the tie. frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.40 p=0.6 [e10] was not monotonic dose-dependent - peak at 1uM not 10uM - inconsistent with classic Aurora dose escalation. More discriminating: nuc_eccentricity rho=+1.00 p=0 [e11] together with nuc_area rho=-1.00 p=0 [e13] - nuclei getting more eccentric and smaller with dose. For Aurora/Eg5/microtubule classes we would expect increased ploidy and large nuclei / increased integrated DNA, and for Eg5/microtubule an increased mitotic fraction. We saw the opposite: frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 p=0.2 not significant [e12], nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.20 p=0.8 flat [e14], frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.20 p=0.8 flat [e15], cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6 no strong cytotoxicity slope [e16], tub_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2 not significant [e17]. Visual checks [e4][e5] noted no bundles/intact network, so we did not rationalize Microtubule stabilizers from tubulin abundance alone - exactly the trap review noted.

That is why update_hypotheses [e18] kept Epithelial 0.68 with Aurora 0.14, Protein synthesis 0.08, Eg5 0.04. We correctly left mass on Aurora given the high multinucleate proxy, but down-weighted it because the ploidy/mitotic readouts contradicted it. We submitted at p=0.68 not >0.90, which was well calibrated for n=4 Spearman with limited power.

What we missed / limitations:

- We only acquired 4 wells and did not sample the lowest doses 0.003-0.01uM. A full 8-point curve would have better defined onset and baseline for eccentricity/area. With n=4, rho p-values 0.6-0.8 are underpowered except for the p=0 monotonic trends.
- Protein synthesis remained 4/10 in k-neighbours [e6][e9] but we had no strong morphologic discriminator for it beyond dose trends; we correctly kept it low at 0.08 but without a translational assay we could not exclude it orthogonally.
- lookup_compound [e20] returned no curated mechanism for AZ-J (BBBC021 internal code, no PubChem/ChEMBL hit), and literature searches for EGFR/epithelial phenotype [e21] and Aurora multinucleation [e22] returned 0 hits in-run, broader search [e23] 21 hits. So external DB/literature could not validate; we relied entirely on atlas + dose trends. That is appropriate but means the "Epithelial" label remains a screening class, not a molecular target - we noted this in conclusion by proposing E-cadherin/beta-catenin membrane localization and EGFR pathway phospho-Western plus live-cell scattering at 0.3,1,10uM with reference controls, not a clinical assay.

Lesson: high z for one striking feature (multinucleate proxy) should be validated against orthogonal quantitative traits - integrated DNA, mitotic fraction, nuclear area direction - and against a multi-dose atlas prior, not read in isolation. No clinical implications inferred.

- Protein synthesis remained 4/10 in k-neighbours [e6][e9] but we had no strong morphologic discriminator for it beyond dose trends; we correctly kept it low at 0.08 but without a translational assay we could not exclude it orthogonally.
- lookup_compound [e20] returned no curated mechanism for AZ-J (BBBC021 internal code, no PubChem/ChEMBL hit), and literature searches for EGFR/epithelial phenotype [e21] and Aurora multinucleation [e22] returned 0 hits in-run, broader search [e23] 21 hits. So external DB/literature could not validate; we relied entirely on atlas + dose trends. That is appropriate but means the "Epithelial" label remains a screening class, not a molecular target - we noted this in conclusion by proposing E-cadherin/beta-catenin membrane localization and EGFR pathway phospho-Western plus live-cell scattering at 0.3,1,10uM with reference controls, not a clinical assay.

Lesson: high z for one striking feature (multinucleate proxy) should be validated against orthogonal quantitative traits - integrated DNA, mitotic fraction, nuclear area direction - and against a multi-dose atlas prior, not read in isolation. No clinical implications inferred.

What was right:
- NSC 4/4 Epithelial persistence [e9]
- monotonic eccentricity increase [e11] and area decrease [e13] vs flat ploidy [e14] and mitotic fraction [e15] rejecting Aurora/Eg5

What was wrong or missed:
- high multinucleate proxy [e2][e3][e7] initially supports Aurora; non-significant tub_mean rise [e17] could trap to microtubule

Proposed next experiment: Proposed E-cadherin/beta-catenin and EGFR phospho-Western plus scattering time-lapse with reference agents at 0.3,1,10uM
